question: A motorcycle "fits" you properly when, at minimum:
choice_a: Your feet can reach the ground while you are seated on it
choice_d: It matches the color of your gear
explanation: First, make sure your motorcycle is right for you -- it should fit you. Your feet should reach the ground while you are seated on the motorcycle.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.8, 'The Right Motorcycle for You'

question: How many mirrors should a street-legal motorcycle have at minimum, according to the handbook?
explanation: At minimum, a street-legal motorcycle should have a headlight, taillight and brakelight, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.9, 'Know Your Motorcycle'

question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes occur on motorcycles ridden by the operator for less than:
explanation: More than half of all crashes occur on motorcycles ridden by the operator for less than six months, so riders should ride extra carefully on any new or unfamiliar motorcycle.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.9, 'Know Your Motorcycle'

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar motorcycle, the handbook advises you to:
choice_a: Ride it immediately in heavy traffic to save time
choice_b: Skip equipment checks since it isn't yours
choice_c: Only check that it has enough fuel
choice_d: Get familiar with it in a controlled area before riding it in traffic
explanation: Crashes are fairly common among beginning riders, and riding an unfamiliar motorcycle adds to the problem. If you borrow a motorcycle, get familiar with it in a controlled area.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.9, 'Borrowing and Lending'

question: If you lend your motorcycle to friends, the handbook says you should make sure they:
choice_a: Are licensed and know how to ride before letting them out into traffic
choice_b: Sign a waiver and nothing more
choice_c: Wear a helmet, but no other protective gear is necessary
choice_d: Have previously owned a motorcycle, regardless of license status
explanation: If you lend your motorcycle to friends, make sure they are licensed and know how to ride before allowing them out into traffic.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.9, 'Borrowing and Lending'

question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should be able to find and operate without looking, in particular:
choice_b: The turn signals, horn, headlight switch, fuel-control valve, and engine cut-off switch
explanation: On an unfamiliar motorcycle, find out where everything is, particularly the turn signals, horn, headlight switch, fuel-control valve, and engine cut-off switch, and operate them without having to look.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.9-10, 'Get Familiar with the Motorcycle Controls'

question: Before mounting the motorcycle as part of the pre-ride check, you should check:
choice_c: Tires, fluids, and the headlights and taillight
explanation: Before mounting the motorcycle, check the tires for air pressure and wear, check oil and fluid levels for leaks, and check that the headlights and taillight work properly.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.10, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: Once you have mounted the motorcycle, before starting out you should check:
choice_d: Clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn
explanation: Once mounted, check that the clutch and throttle work smoothly, clean and adjust both mirrors, try the front and rear brakes, and try the horn before starting out.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.10-11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: In addition to the checks made before every trip, which items should be checked at least once a week?
choice_a: Wheels, cables, fasteners, and fluid levels
choice_b: Only tire tread, once a month
explanation: In addition to the checks you make before every trip, check wheels, cables, fasteners and fluid levels at least once a week, following your owner's manual for recommendations.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: How should you adjust your mirrors before riding?
choice_a: So they show only your own shoulder
choice_b: So you can see the lane behind and as much as possible of the lane next to you
choice_c: So they are angled toward the sky
choice_d: So they show only the front wheel
explanation: Adjust each mirror so you can see the lane behind and as much as possible of the lane next to you; it's the road behind and to the side that matters most.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.10, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: Regarding crashes in traffic, the handbook explains that:
choice_a: Crashes are entirely random and unforeseeable events
choice_b: One party is always solely at fault
choice_c: Most people involved in a crash can usually claim some responsibility for what took place
choice_d: A rider's own behavior cannot reduce crash risk
explanation: "Accident" implies an unforeseen event without anyone's fault, but that is not usually the case in traffic -- most people involved in a crash can usually claim some responsibility.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: To lessen the chances of a crash, the handbook advises riders to:
choice_a: Ride only at night to avoid traffic
choice_b: Avoid using turn signals so as not to distract other drivers
choice_c: Ride as close as possible to surrounding vehicles
choice_d: Be visible, communicate intentions, and maintain an adequate space cushion
explanation: To lessen your chances of a crash, be visible, communicate your intentions, maintain an adequate space cushion, scan ahead, and be prepared to act.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: According to the handbook, how many seconds ahead should a rider scan their path of travel?
explanation: As part of reducing crash risk, riders should scan their path of travel 12 seconds ahead.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: When facing multiple hazards at once, a responsible rider should:
choice_a: Focus only on the nearest hazard and ignore the rest
choice_b: Identify and separate the hazards, and remain prepared to act
choice_c: Accelerate to clear all hazards simultaneously
choice_d: Come to a complete stop regardless of traffic behind
explanation: Responsible riding includes identifying and separating multiple hazards and being prepared to act -- remaining alert and knowing how to carry out crash-avoidance skills.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: Even if another driver is first to start the chain of events leading to a crash, the handbook states that:
choice_a: The other driver is always entirely at fault
choice_b: The rider bears no responsibility whatsoever
choice_c: It doesn't leave any of us free of responsibility
choice_d: Only a court can assign any responsibility
explanation: Just because someone else is the first to start the chain of events leading to a crash, it doesn't leave any of us free of responsibility.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.11, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: To add a motorcycle endorsement to an existing North Carolina driver's license, an applicant must:
choice_a: Simply pay a fee, with no testing required
choice_c: Complete a mail-in form with no in-person requirement
choice_d: Take a knowledge test that includes motorcycling questions and an off-street motorcycle skills test
explanation: The law requires the operator of a motorcycle to have an endorsement, obtained by taking a knowledge test that includes questions on motorcycling and an off-street motorcycle skills test.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.5, 'Licensing and Registration'

question: According to the handbook, the motorcycle knowledge test is waived:
choice_d: It is never waived under any circumstance
explanation: The knowledge test will be waived on a renewal, but is otherwise required to obtain a motorcycle endorsement.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.5, 'Licensing and Registration'

question: A rider not yet prepared for the skills portion of the test, but who holds a full provisional, regular, or commercial license, may apply for:
explanation: If you are not prepared to take the skills portion of the test, you may apply for a motorcycle learner permit if you possess a full provisional, regular, or commercial license.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.5, 'Licensing and Registration'
